newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro Disney repeats caution on outlook.
newsitem.headline: Euro Disney repeats caution on outlook.

text.p: Euro Disney SCA, the operator of the Disneyland Paris theme park, sounded a cautious note about current year and future results as the company assumes expenses suspended as part of a 1993 debt restructuring.

Lease and financial expenses in fiscal 1996 totalled 568 million francs, up 103 million from the previous year "and will continue to increase during the next fiscal years -- by approximately an additional 200 million francs in fiscal year 1997 and an additional 120 million francs in fiscal year 1998," supervisory board chairman Antoine Jeancourt-Galignani said in a letter to shareholders in Euro Disney's annual report.
"From fiscal year 1999, the payment of royalties and management fees to The Walt Disney Co (39 percent shareholder) will begin to have a significant impact on...results."
Management board chairman Philippe Bourguignon reiterated that 1997 would be "a more challenging year" than fiscal 1996, when its net profits rose 77 percent to 202 million francs.

Even as financial expenses rise, "the general context of reduced tourist spending, the strength of the French franc relative to other currencies and the price sensitivity of our product are not allowing us to increase prices," he said.

"Based on current projections, management believes that it has the resources necessary to meet funding requirements arising in fiscal year 1997. However, long-term liquidity requirements of the company include the redemption and/or refinancing of the remaining 6.75 percent convertible bonds upon maturity on October 1, 2001," the annual report said.
Despite its cautious tone, Euro Disney underscored the popular success of its European theme park and said Disneyland Paris had attracted close to 50 million visitors in less than five years.
